name: TeslaMate
author: simbesh; original plugin by Jankees van Woezik
description: TeslaMate MQTT vehicle status, location and navigation

barWidget.description: TeslaMate MQTT vehicle status, location and navigation

schema.label: Status bar display
schema.description: Choose battery charge (57%), rated range (240km), or just the Tesla icon.

schema.label: Map
schema.description: Tiles come from OpenStreetMap, which needs no account. It ships one style and it is a pale one, so Dark is that same map inverted and turned half a colour wheel, the way OpenStreetMap's own site does its dark mode: water stays blue, parks stay green, and the paper goes black. Auto follows your theme, because a light map inside a dark panel is a torch in the face and a dark one inside a light panel is a hole in it.

schema.label: Zoom
schema.description: 16 shows the street the car is on and the ones either side, which is the level at which you can tell whether it is where you left it. Lower to see which town, higher to see which parking space.

schema.label: Panel width
schema.description: In the shell's spacing units. The map is this wide and everything else is measured off it, so this one number sizes the whole panel. Anything wider than the screen is trimmed to fit.

schema.label: Look the position up by name
schema.description: Turns the coordinates into a street and a town, through OpenStreetMap's Nominatim. Answers are cached per position, so a parked car is one lookup however often you look at it. Off if you would rather nothing but Tesla learned where the car is.

schema.label: Tell me when the car pulls away
schema.description: A desktop notification the moment a reading says the car has gone from parked to driving, the same moment the mark in the bar turns green. Only for a departure this widget watched happen: a car already moving when the bar starts is not news.

schema.label: Where a click on the map goes
schema.description: The address opened when you click the map, with {lat} and {lon} standing in for the position. Google Maps by default because that is what most people navigate with; https://www.openstreetmap.org/?mlat={lat}&mlon={lon}#map=17/{lat}/{lon} keeps it in OpenStreetMap.
